subject: Post-demo: Hyperscaler comparison + private/VPC tech-spike plan
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@payments-inc.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo today — quick follow-up and clarification requests

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the demo earlier. Good discussion; a few things the infra team asked me to put in writing so we can scope a short tech spike: 

- High level ask: we want an apples-to-apples latency and throughput comparison vs the three big clouds' managed inference endpoints (BigCloud, Hyperscale A, Hyperscale B). Our evaluation needs to include a private/VPC deployment option (we may need the control plane inside our VPC or an on-prem path) and confirm whether your offering can be air-gapped for certification later.

- Networking questions: do you support cross-account VPC peering, direct connect equivalents, and are there fixed egress IP ranges we can whitelist? We need a firewall/IP allowlist for the spike.

- Test acceptance criteria: p95 latency under 200ms for our 2K token prompt, sustained 25 QPS (for the model size we discussed), and deterministic cold-start behavior (time to first token). Also, we need logs/audit evidence for data residency (no customer data persists in hosted control plane).

Can you propose a concise test matrix, list of artifacts we should expect (benchmarks, billing rundown, network config), and propose 2-3 dates for the spike? I've looped in Rajat from our platform team for networking follow-up.

Thanks —
Alice Chen
Head of Platform Engineering
Payments, Inc.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@payments-inc.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo today — quick follow-up and clarification requests

Alice —

Really appreciate the clear follow-up and the acceptance criteria. Summary and proposed plan below (short and actionable):

1) Objective — short tech spike (3 business days) to run controlled side-by-side tests against BigCloud/Hyperscale A/B plus a Redwood private/VPC deployment. Deliverables: raw latency/throughput CSVs, p95/p99 summaries, cold-start traces, network diagram, and a post-spike recommendation (cost/latency tradeoffs).

2) Test matrix (attached: redwood-hyperscaler-test-matrix.xlsx) — key vectors:
   - Model variant parity (same weights where possible; otherwise nearest-open equivalent)
   - Sequence len: 2k tokens (prompt+response)
   - Workloads: steady-state QPS (5, 10, 25), burst (100 concurrent short requests), cold-start (instance spin-up + first token)
   - Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, egress bandwidth, CPU/GPU utilization, KV-cache hit-rate, cost-per-1K-tokens (approx)

3) Private/VPC specifics — we can run the inference runtime in your VPC with either: 
   - Dedicated tenant-hosted control plane (customer-managed in VPC) OR
   - Redwood-hosted control plane with private networking (VPC peering or direct connect) and strict audit controls.

    Notes: the fully air-gapped on-prem option is supported but requires a short deployment runbook and an ops window for installation. Air-gap certification (no outbound connectivity) is feasible — we'll need a build of our control plane artifacts to be delivered and a short on-site/remote install.

4) Networking asks (what we need from Payments, Inc.):
   - Firewall/IP allowlist (we maintain static egress ranges for dedicated customers)
   - A platform contact with ability to create VPC peering or a Direct Connect/L2 tunnel (Rajat? +1)
   - Access to a small test subnet and optional bastion for debugging (temporary credentials)

5) Proposed timing:
   - Tech spike window options: Dec 1–3, Dec 6–8, Dec 9–11 (3 business-day windows). Plan to lock one after we confirm network prerequisites.

6) Next steps (mutual action plan):
   - Payments: confirm preferred window + provide firewall/IP doc and networking contact.
   - Redwood: provision private pool, prepare benchmark harness, run baseline tests vs public endpoints, and deliver results and short recommendation.

Attachments: redwood-hyperscaler-test-matrix.xlsx, tech-spike-schedule.ics (calendar candidate slots).

I'm copying Vanessa (Senior Solutions Engineer) to handle the bench details and Marissa for success/ops coordination. Vanessa — can you review the matrix and confirm the test VM types and whether we'll need an on-site install package for the air-gapped run?

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodai.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@payments-inc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo today — quick follow-up and clarification requests

Alice / Karthik —

Quick technical confirmations and clarifications from the bench perspective:

- Hyperscaler parity: we will aim to use the same open model (or closest quantized equivalent) across all endpoints. Note that hyperscalers often run different inference stacks and may impose their own JVM/TF optimizations; we'll call that out in the results.

- Egress / IP ranges: for a Dedicated/private pool we can provide a fixed egress CIDR block (three /29s) you can whitelist. I'll attach a formal PDF with the ranges once we lock the window. For the hosted control-plane + private networking option, egress for inference traffic still originates from your VPC.

- Control-plane residency: Two patterns: (A) customer-managed control plane (we deliver container images + orchestration manifests you run in your VPC/on-prem) — suitable for air-gapped certification; (B) Redwood-managed control plane inside a dedicated VPC peered to yours (shorter lead time). Option A requires an operations window (~4 hours) and a handful of ports open for our installer; Option B requires peering and allowlist.

- Bench sizing / hardware parity: we'll provision a dedicated p4-equivalent instance for Redwood private and attempt to request like-for-like GPUs on BigCloud. If hyperscalers cannot provide the identical card, we'll document the delta and run a normalized cost/latency curve (tokens/sec per GPU FLOPS).

- Data residency & logs: during the spike we can enable verbose audit logs and (if requested) an export bundle showing request hashes only (no plaintext payloads) to prove control-plane does not persist customer data. For compliance later, we can provide an architecture diagram and a SOC2-scope playbook.

Proposed concrete asks from Payments, Inc. (short):
  1) Confirm which control-plane residency you prefer (A or B).
  2) Provide the networking contact + firewall/IP doc.
  3) Pick one tech-spike window.

I'll prepare the egress CIDR PDF and the test harness repo link after we pick a window. If you want, we can run a 30-minute pre-spike call with your platform team to walk through the VPC peering steps — recommend scheduling that 48 hours before the spike.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Rajat Singh <rajat.s@platform-eng.bigcloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@payments-inc.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2026 19:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Demo today — quick follow-up and clarification requests

Vanessa / Karthik —

Thanks — attaching the firewall doc you requested (Payments-inc-firewall-ips.pdf). Payments prefers option B (Redwood-managed control plane in a peered VPC) to reduce ops overhead for the spike. Dec 6–8 works best for our team. We'll schedule the pre-spike 30-min run-through on Dec 4 at 10:00 PT.

Firewall doc attached. Rajat (platform) will be our point for peering. Expect me to share a temporary bastion key for debugging during the window.

Rajat Singh
Principal Platform Engineer
Payments, Inc.
